$comment: Four-role Postgres credential split (root/owner/app/ro) across projects.
Vault items are GROUPED per tier (vault scopes the project, the title the tier,
one field per principal):
op://<PROJECT>-sensitive/Postgres prod/{root|owner|app|<app-slug>|<app-slug>_migrator}
op://<PROJECT>/Postgres prod RO/{canonical|<app-slug>}   (ro principals)
op://<PROJECT>/Postgres staging/{root|owner|app|ro|<app-slug>|<app-slug>_ro|<app-slug>_migrator}
Vault routing (Amaru policy): prod write -> <PROJECT>-sensitive; prod RO + all
staging -> <PROJECT> regular (SA-readable). admin_refs[tier].{root,owner} name the
box's provider-default login ('root') and admin owner fields explicitly (no convention
fallback). 'root' is only Render's databaseUser — Render managed Postgres has no actual
superuser, so the root field is never a superuser escape hatch.
Postgres login names always include the project slug (roles are catalog-global;
Workflow + Autodev share dpg-d66ig… so collisions matter).
Root username is the Render provider default and is NOT renamed; root and the
table owner are never rotation predecessors.
Per-app principals: projects[].apps.<app-slug> declares one login set per
application (roles.app / .ro / .migrator); the app slug is the vault field name
(item_prefix = SLUG_ for tooling that still prefixes env names).
instance: 'default' (own project's tiers) or {project, tier_map} for cross-instance
consumers — the role is created on the OWNING project's box (admin via its owner
credential) but the vault item is written into the CONSUMER project's vault.
databases: optional override of which databases the grants (and the item URL's
primary db) target; default is the tier database plus extra_databases.
ts_scraper and ts_decrypt_proxy have NO DB rows in their manifests (checked
2026-08-07) — deliberately absent from ts.apps.

amaru_mcp.note: prod only: no staging amaru-mcp service exists (staging AMARU_MCP_ENABLED=false).

prod.notes: Render databaseUser is ts_root (ROOT item). Application tables are owned by ts_user; Render owner credential membership targets ts_user.

workflow_mcp.note: prod only (srv-d9it0j37uimc73c49cfg); SYSTEM_DATABASE_URL stays on workflow_owner.

autodev.shared_instance_note: Same Render Postgres as workflow-pro prod (dpg-d66ig…). Creating a Render credential would flip the instance default away from workflow_owner — so autodev_owner is a SQL role provisioned as the shared admin, not a Render credential. Root remains the instance admin (render).

autodev_dashboard.note: app (not ro): the dashboard performs writes (semantic mutations, human commands). Grants span mem_autodev + mem_global + mem_workflow_pro (tier database + extra_databases).

autodev_memory.note: migrator: boot-time Alembic (scripts/migrate_all.py) across mem_autodev + mem_global + mem_workflow_pro. Member of autodev_owner (sql_role SET ROLE target). GRANT render is impossible (no ADMIN OPTION on render); provision REASSIGNs mem_* objects from render to autodev_owner so ALTER TABLE works. Independent of autodev_memory_app: rotating this does not rewrite DATABASE_URL_*.

autodev_mem_ts.note: SQL role on the TS prod box (admin via ts owner credential); item written into the AUTODEV vault — the consumer owns its credential. migrator on the TS prod box for mem_ts. Provisioned via the ts owner credential, stored in the AUTODEV vault: autodev owns the credential it runs with, so a TS owner rotation can never strand autodev-memory. ro: read-only principal for the autodev-dashboard schema-drift CI gate against mem_ts, replacing the borrowed op://TS/Postgres prod RO/canonical.

autodev_mem_amaru.note: SQL role on the Amaru prod box (admin via amaru owner credential); item written into the AUTODEV vault. migrator on the Amaru prod box for mem_amaru. Provisioned via the amaru owner credential, stored in the AUTODEV vault (same ownership rule as mem_ts).
